title: Masi bark cloth stencil printing
summary: Fijian masi is beaten bark cloth printed with cut stencils: dye is rubbed through the openings in black and rust-brown to build bold bands of triangles, diamonds and zigzags. Copy the pattern, which mirrors both ways.
howToPlay: Pick a dye and a stencil shape.
Place it; the mirrored copies print too.
Check the cloth against the pattern.
Watch and learn shows a finished round, one placement at a time.
rules: The cloth mirrors left to right and top to bottom.
Placing the same shape in the same colour again, or choosing the eraser, clears it and its mirror partners.
The result compares your piece with the pattern cell by cell: three stars at 98 percent or more, two at 85, one at 60.
The pattern to copy is always shown beside the work and as a faint guide on the cloth.
heritageNote: Masi is the bark cloth of Fiji, beaten from the inner bark of the paper mulberry and decorated with stencils and dye. Makers and communities keep the craft alive for everyday use and for gifts.
credits: Pattern designs are original arrangements in the tradition's motif vocabulary.
